claims.text: Interface-induced strain disrupts the cooperative magnetostructural transition in as-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi-type films or nanoribbons.
The cooperative magnetostructural transition underlies the strong magnetocaloric response reported in bulk FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys.
Controlled thermal annealing will relieve interface-induced strain in the nanoscale material.
Relieving interface-induced strain will partially restore a bulk-like magnetocaloric effect.
Relieving interface-induced strain will reduce hysteresis during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Annealing at approximately 400 °C for 30 minutes in an inert atmosphere will reduce defect concentrations.
Film/substrate interfaces and patterned edges produce nonuniform lattice parameters.
Nonuniform lattice parameters hamper cooperative magnetic and structural reordering.
Annealing-induced strain relief enhances cooperative magnetic ordering.
Annealing-induced strain relief enhances heat transport.
A more uniform transformation narrows cycle hysteresis.
Post-annealing samples will exhibit a larger temperature change or entropy change during low-field magnetic cooling than the as-deposited baseline.
Post-annealing samples will exhibit a narrower hysteresis loop than the as-deposited baseline.
The as-deposited state has diminished magnetocaloric performance because of persistent interface-induced strain and lattice defects.
The as-deposited state has broader hysteresis because of persistent interface-induced strain and lattice defects.
The proposed behavior applies to films thicker than about 20 nm or patterned nanoribbons when interface strain is significant.
Ultra-thin samples below about 20 nm may not exhibit the predicted annealing response.
Cycling above the heat-transfer-limited frequency may prevent the predicted behavior.
